text: Welcome to this short lesson on FastAPI dependency injection. By the end you'll know what dependencies are and how to use them.
In FastAPI a dependency is just a function or callable that returns something your route needs, like a database session or the current user.
You declare a dependency by adding a parameter to your path operation and wrapping it with Depends. FastAPI resolves it before calling your function.
For example, def get_db opens a session, yields it, and closes it in a finally block. You then write db: Session = Depends(get_db) in the route.
Because get_db uses yield, the code after the yield runs as teardown after the response is sent. This is how FastAPI handles cleanup safely.
Dependencies can depend on other dependencies. get_current_user can itself depend on get_db and on an oauth2 token scheme, forming a small graph.
FastAPI caches a dependency within a single request by default, so if two parts of the request need get_db, the same session is reused.
You can disable that caching by passing use_cache equals false to Depends when you genuinely need a fresh instance each time.
Dependencies are great for authentication, database sessions, rate limiting, and shared query parameters, keeping your route functions clean.
You can also attach dependencies at the router or app level so they run for every endpoint, which is useful for global auth checks.
To recap: a dependency is a callable, you inject it with Depends, yield enables setup and teardown, and dependencies can be nested and cached per request.
